([[Macomb Township, Michigan]]) | college = [[Toledo Rockets men's basketball|Toledo]] (2020–present) | highlights = * First-team All-[[Mid-American Conference|MAC]] (2022) * MAC Freshman of the Year (2021) * MAC All-Freshman Team (2021) }} '''Ryan Anthony Rollins''' (born July 3, 2002) is an American [[college basketball]] player for the [[Toledo Rockets men's basketball|Toledo Rockets]] of the [[Mid-American Conference]] (MAC). ==Early life and high school career== Rollins was born and raised in [[Detroit|Detroit, Michigan]].{{cite web |last1=Murray |first1=Derek |title=2022 NBA Draft Q&A: Toledo's Ryan Rollins is 'the guy you want' |url=https://www.basketballnews.com/stories/2022-nba-draft-qa-toledos-ryan-rollins |publisher=Basketball News |access-date=June 14, 2022 |date=May 26, 2022}} He played basketball for [[Dakota High School (Michigan)|Dakota High School]] in [[Macomb Township, Michigan]]. As a junior, he averaged 17.1 points, 7 rebounds, 3.2 assists and 2.5 steals per game, missing the second half of the season with a hamstring injury.{{cite web |last1=Purcell |first1=Jared |title=Dakota’s Ryan Rollins more concerned with playoff run than Mr. Basketball |url=https://www.mlive.com/highschoolsports/2020/02/dakotas-ryan-rollins-more-concerned-with-playoff-run-than-mr-basketball.html |publisher=MLive |access-date=June 13, 2022 |date=February 5, 2020}} In his senior season, Rollins averaged 25.5 points, nine rebounds and five assists per game, earning second-team All-State honors from the [[Associated Press]]. A three-star [[college recruiting|recruit]], he committed to playing college basketball for [[Toledo Rockets men's basketball|Toledo]] after the program prioritized him early in the recruiting process.{{cite web |last1=Buckey |first1=Brian |title=Incoming point guard Rollins ready to learn the ropes at Toledo |url=https://www.toledoblade.com/sports/ut/2020/06/04/incoming-point-guard-ryan-rollins-ready-to-learn-the-ropes-at-toledo/stories/20200604091 |website=[[The Blade (Toledo, Ohio)|The Blade]] |access-date=June 13, 2022 |date=June 4, 2020}} ==College career== Rollins immediately made an impact as a freshman at Toledo.{{cite web |last1=Rowland |first1=Kyle |title=UT freshman Rollins plays like a veteran |url=https://www.toledoblade.com/sports/ut/2021/03/08/UT-freshman-Rollins-plays-like-a-veteran/stories/20210308022 |website=[[The Blade (Toledo, Ohio)|The Blade]] |access-date=June 14, 2022 |date=March 8, 2021}} He averaged 13.7 points, 5.2 rebounds and 2.5 assists per game, and was named [[Mid-American Conference]] (MAC) Freshman of the Year after helping his team win the MAC regular season title.{{cite web |last1=Rowland |first1=Kyle |title=UT's Rollins will keep name in NBA draft |url=https://www.toledoblade.com/sports/ut/2022/05/31/ut-s-rollins-will-keep-name-in-nba-draft/stories/20220531137 |website=[[The Blade (Toledo, Ohio)|The Blade]] |access-date=June 14, 2022 |date=May 31, 2022}} Rollins assumed a leading role in his sophomore season with the transfer of [[Marreon Jackson]].{{cite web |last1=Sansom |first1=Jordan |title=Toledo Rockets star Ryan Rollins looks to take the next step in his game |url=https://bvmsports.com/2021/12/13/toledo-rockets-star-ryan-rollins-looks-to-take-the-next-step-in-his-game/ |publisher=BVM Sports |access-date=June 14, 2022 |date=December 13, 2021}} On November 24, 2021, he scored a career-high 35 points in a 79–70 victory over [[Coastal Carolina Chanticleers men's basketball|Coastal Carolina]] to win the [[Nassau Championship]], where he was named tournament [[most valuable player]].{{cite web |last1=French |first1=Simba |title=Rockets wins inaugural ‘Nassau Championship’ |url=https://thenassauguardian.com/rockets-wins-inaugural-nassau-championship/ |website=[[The Nassau Guardian]] |access-date=June 14, 2022 |date=November 26, 2021}} Rollins helped Toledo repeat as MAC regular season champions.{{cite web |title=Toledo Claims Share of MAC Regular Season Title |url=https://getsomemaction.com/news/2022/3/1/mens-basketball-toledo-claims-share-of-mac-regular-season-title.aspx |publisher=[[Mid-American Conference]] |access-date=June 14, 2022 |date=March 1, 2022}} As a sophomore, he averaged 18.9 points, six rebounds and 3.6 assists per game, earning first-team All-MAC honors. He opted to remain in the [[2022 NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining college eligibility. ==Personal life== Rollins' brother, Chris, played [[college basketball]] for [[Davenport Panthers|Davenport]].{{cite web |last1=Evans |first1=Jim |title=A little R&R: Dakota hoops star Ryan Rollins signs with Toledo |url=https://www.macombdaily.com/2019/11/18/a-little-rr-dakota-hoops-star-ryan-rollins-signs-with-toledo/ |website=[[The Macomb Daily]] |access-date=June 13, 2022 |date=November 18, 2019}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[https://utrockets.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/ryan-rollins/7490 Toledo Rockets bio] [[Category:2002 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players from Detroit]] [[Category:Shooting guards]] [[Category:Toledo Rockets men's basketball players]]
